facts.fact_text: Both applicants participated in the political rally on 6 May 2012.

According to an internal inquiry conducted in the aftermath of the events at Bolotnaya Square, a police officer had called the first applicant (Mr Zakharov), inviting him to come to the police station to give further information and identify the police officer responsible for the attack.
The report on the internal inquiry conducted in the aftermath of the events at Bolotnaya Square was dated 8 June 2012.

The report on the internal inquiry dated 8 June 2012 stated that the first applicant (Mr Zakharov) had refused to attend the meeting at the police station, stating that he could not identify the police officer concerned.
The investigator at the Zamoskvoretskiy branch of the Investigation Committee did not examine the incident in respect of the first applicant (Mr Zakharov) in his decision of 20 March 2013.
The first applicant (Mr Zakharov) argued that the investigator had not addressed his allegations in the decision of 20 March 2013.
The first applicant (Mr Zakharov) argued that the investigator had made no attempt to identify the police officer responsible for the attack on him.
The first applicant (Mr Zakharov) claimed that by joining his application to those of others, the investigator had avoided assessing the particular incident of which he had complained.

The first applicant (Mr Zakharov) disputed what had allegedly been said during the telephone call in June 2012 in which a police officer had invited him to come to the police station to identify the officer responsible for the attack.
The second applicant (Ms Varzhabetyan) argued that the numerous remittals of the case for further inquiries revealed the deficiency of the work of the investigators.
